newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X says Busang permits in good standing.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says Busang permits in good standing.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Thursday that its officials met with Indonesian mining officials in Jakarta and were assured its exploration permits and contract of work applications remain in good standing.

Bre-X officials Rolando Francisco and John Felderhof met earlier Thursday with Umar Said, secretary general of the ministry of mines and energy, to clarify outstanding issues relating to Bre-X's huge Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
Umar apologized for comments about the cancelation of exploration permits and contract of work (CoW) applications for its Busang II and III gold prospects, Bre-X said.
"The exploration permits and CoW applications for Busang II and III remain in good standing," Bre-X said in a statement issued from Jakarta.
It was the third news release from Bre-X in as many hours.
"Obviously significant progress is being made on all fronts towards development of the Busang deposit," Bre-X chief executive David Walsh said in the statement.
"Shareholders must be as pleased as we are with the recent developments."
He said allegations passed on to Reuters in Jakarta on Wednesday were "erroneous and without foundation."

The CoWs for Busang II and III are crucial for Bre-X. The properties, on the island of Borneo in the Indonesian province of East Kalimantan, are the richest parts of the Busang deposit, estimated to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.

Earlier on Thursday, Umar told Reuters for the second time in two days that Bre-X's applications for CoWs to develop Busang had been canceled. He said Bre-X and Barrick Gold Corp must form a joint venture company and submit new applications for CoWs.
Toronto-based Barrick and Bre-X are in the midst of negotiations to form a joint venture company.
But Bre-X expressed hope in one of two earlier press releases issued on Thursday that Indonesian President Suharto would open up the negotiation process for Busang.
"We're not soliciting other offers. We are getting other phone calls," Walsh said. "I am talking to the principals of other companies."
He said he had spoken to executives at Vancouver-based Placer Dome Inc, Newmont Mining Corp NEM.TO and Teck Corp.
Barrick, meanwhile, said it was still seeking clarity about Bre-X's rights to Busang.
"We're still seeking clarification and we want to hear directly from the government of Indonesia," Barrick spokesman Vince Borg told Reuters.
